thread:
Maya (PM): Heads up — we need a crisp policy for automatic fallback that balances latency SLOs and customer SLAs. Current canary rolls are fine but when tail errors spike we're seeing noisy rollbacks.
Alex (Eng): Agree. Proposal: a circuit-breaker-like policy that can flip degrade modes automatically based on two signals: error rate (5m window) and p95 latency (1m window).
Sam (Platform): +1. What degrade modes are we considering? We should keep them composable.
Maya (PM): Suggested modes: 1) serve-from-cache (fast failover), 2) reduced-token-budget (lower max tokens), 3) cheap-model-fallback (smaller quantized variant), 4) reject-with-grace (structured error + retry-after).
Priya (UX): From console POV we need to show which mode is active, why (signal), and a quick button to "force rollback" or "override" with audit reason. Also breadcrumbs for the sequence of mode switches.
Luis (SRE): Signals we can reliably get: 5xx rate per route, request timeout rate, infra OOMs, and queue depth. Important: avoid flapping. We should require both error rate > X AND p95 > Y OR error budget burn > Z to trigger.
Alex (Eng): Draft policy config (example):
```json
{
  "triggers": {
    "error_rate": {"window": "5m", "threshold": 0.03},
    "p95_latency_ms": {"window": "1m", "threshold": 1200}
  },
  "logic": "(error_rate > t1 && p95_latency_ms > t2) || error_budget_burn > t3",
  "degrade_sequence": ["serve-from-cache", "cheap-model-fallback", "reduced-token-budget"],
  "min_hold": "60s",
  "cooldown": "5m"
}
```
Sam (Platform): Nice. A couple notes: 1) 'serve-from-cache' requires warm caches + prefix-keying for multi-tenant workloads; 2) cheap-model-fallback needs model-compatibility checks in routing.
Maya (PM): For audit we need immutable events for: trigger-eval, mode-enter, mode-exit, manual-override. Each event should record policy-id, matched-signal-values, and the active rollout id.
Priya (UX): Console mock: small timeline on route page showing colored segments (green = normal, amber = degraded, red = rejected). Hover shows trigger details + link to playback logs. Also a compact toast when a mode flips: "Auto-degraded to cheap-model-fallback (error_rate=4.1%) — [View details] [Override]"
Luis (SRE): We should log raw telemetry to an append-only audit stream (kafka) and index metadata for quick querying. Also attach a compact snapshot of perf counters at trigger time.
Alex (Eng): Implementation plan: 1) policy evaluator service (stateless) polls metrics + computes triggers, 2) publish mode command to routing control-plane, 3) routing agents subscribe and apply mode via flag. Backoff logic lives in evaluator.
Sam (Platform): API shape for teams: POST /v1/routes/:id/auto-fallbacks { policy: <json>, enabled: true } GET /v1/routes/:id/auto-fallbacks/actions -> history. Need RBAC for enabling.
Maya (PM): Success criteria: fewer noisy rollbacks, measurable reduction in customer errors during infra incidents, and no increased unintended rejections. We'll run a staged rollout on low-risk routes.
Priya (UX): For the override flow, capture user reason and link to incident/PR. Keep the override auditable and auto-expire after the route is healthy.
Alex (Eng): One edge-case: what if cheap-model-fallback has higher hallucination rate? We need an evaluation fallback whitelist for routes that can tolerate quality drop. Add 'quality_tolerance' field to policy.
Luis (SRE): Also add a "dry-run" flag that logs what the policy would have done without actually flipping modes. We'll run dry-run for 48h before enabling.
deploy-bot: deploy started for feature/auto-fallback-eval -> canary to infra-test cluster
Maya (PM): Action items: Alex to draft API + evaluator proto, Sam to spec RBAC + telemetry schema, Priya to mock console and toast, Luis to design audit stream. We'll reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:
